headline: Gas emerges from submersible pump in Gopalganj, ignites into flames
summary: A submersible pump in Kotali Para, Gopalganj, is releasing gas along with water, causing curiosity among locals who are calling for an expert team to investigate.
details: In Kotali Para, Gopalganj, a submersible pump is releasing gas along with water. When a lighter or match is held to the pipe, the gas ignites into flames, drawing large crowds of curious locals.
The pump, installed by hardware businessman Kamrul Sheikh up to 280 feet deep, was originally used to supply water to fish transport vehicles.
Sheikh noticed a decrease in water output over the last week. On Wednesday night, out of curiosity, he held a lighter to the pipe, and the gas ignited into flames.
Local residents have expressed their hope that if natural gas is found underground, it would be beneficial for the country.
Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) Saif-ul-Arefin has confirmed the incident. He has already sent Tahsildars to the site and plans to visit the site on Friday to take further action.
caption:
Water pump releases gas that ignites into flames in Gopalganj!

In Kotali Para, Gopalganj, a submersible pump is releasing gas along with water. When a lighter or match is held to the pipe, the gas ignites into flames, drawing large crowds of curious locals.

The pump, installed by hardware businessman Kamrul Sheikh up to 280 feet deep, was originally used to supply water to fish transport vehicles.

Sheikh noticed a decrease in water output over the last week. On Wednesday night, out of curiosity, he held a lighter to the pipe, and the gas ignited into flames.

Local residents have expressed their hope that if natural gas is found underground, it would be beneficial for the country.

Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) Saif-ul-Arefin has confirmed the incident. He has already sent Tahsildars to the site and plans to visit the site on Friday to take further action.

headline_marked: 111 injury marks: [[Ex-SI Akbar sentenced to death]] for custodial murder
headline: 111 injury marks: Ex-SI Akbar sentenced to death for custodial murder
summary: A Sylhet court has sentenced a dismissed police sub-inspector to death and five others to prison for the 2020 torture and killing of Raihan Ahmed.
details: A Sylhet Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court has sentenced dismissed police sub-inspector Akbar Hossain Bhuiyan to death for the murder of Raihan Ahmed.
The court also sentenced two other suspects to life imprisonment and three others to seven years in prison, including a journalist, for their roles in the case.
Raihan, 34, was brought to the Bandarbazar Police Outpost on October 10, 2020, where he was tortured by police personnel, including the outpost's chief, Akbar.
A postmortem report revealed 111 injury marks on Raihan's body, consisting of 97 bruises and 14 severe injuries.
Raihan died the following morning at Sylhet Osmani Medical College Hospital after the torture.
The case was filed by Raihan's wife, Tahmina Akter, under the Torture and Custodial Death (Prevention) Act.
An inquiry committee of the Sylhet Metropolitan Police later confirmed that Raihan had been tortured while in custody at the outpost.
Authorities had suspended four personnel, including SI Akbar, shortly after the incident in October 2020.
caption:
111 injury marks were found on his body. A dismissed police officer has now been sentenced to death for the custodial torture and killing of Raihan Ahmed.

A Sylhet Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court has sentenced dismissed police sub-inspector Akbar Hossain Bhuiyan to death for the murder of Raihan Ahmed.

The court also sentenced two other suspects to life imprisonment and three others to seven years in prison, including a journalist, for their roles in the case.

Raihan, 34, was brought to the Bandarbazar Police Outpost on October 10, 2020, where he was tortured by police personnel, including the outpost's chief, Akbar.

A postmortem report revealed 111 injury marks on Raihan's body, consisting of 97 bruises and 14 severe injuries.

Raihan died the following morning at Sylhet Osmani Medical College Hospital after the torture.

The case was filed by Raihan's wife, Tahmina Akter, under the Torture and Custodial Death (Prevention) Act.

An inquiry committee of the Sylhet Metropolitan Police later confirmed that Raihan had been tortured while in custody at the outpost.

Authorities had suspended four personnel, including SI Akbar, shortly after the incident in October 2020.
